checks.fidelity: SemilocallySimplyConnected is Hatcher's definition (a neighbourhood U of y in which every loop at y is null in Y). It is not vacuous: SemilocallySimplyConnected.of_simplyConnectedSpace holds, and an audit example instantiates isCoveringMap_proj and deckEquiv at Y = R. The topology is generateFrom of B(c,U) over open U, which is a genuine basis (isTopologicalBasis). proj is the endpoint map, not a trivialising definition. The fibre over y0 injects into pi_1, which is used in countability and deckHom_injective. Every hypothesis carried is used, and the dropped ones (connected, Hausdorff, anything on E) really are unnecessary. The universal property is stated for C(.,E) with exists-unique, and the lift is moreover a covering (isCoveringMap_of_comp_eq) and onto for path-connected E. Deck p is the subgroup {phi : E homeo E | p o phi = p}, with deckHom_apply exposing the explicit action. The :1156 equivalence is proved for path-connected plus LPC Y, which is equivalent to the paper's connected plus LPC.

issues.problem: REPORT says 'The paper does not state a composition result, so this is not a defect of the paper'. That is false. The proof of prop:branched_covering_composition, direction (ii)=>(i) (RamcovGX.tex:1137), concludes '(q o p)|X_1^Z_1 is a composition of covering hence a covering' with no finiteness of fibres and no semilocal hypothesis on Z_1, which is only an open portly subset of a connected LPC Hausdorff space. The composite of coverings is not a covering in general; the docstring asserts this but nothing proves it. The only version supplied (finite fibres of the second map) cannot serve :1137, since branched coverings there have infinite fibres. The master session is therefore told there is no paper issue where there is a potential DEC-27 gap in a proof another package must formalize.
issues.fix: Correct the finding. The paper uses the unrestricted composition at :1137 (and builds a composition at :1123). Flag it for the prop:branched_covering_composition package as a possible missing hypothesis. Ideally also add the second standard true variant (Z locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected implies p o q is a covering) and/or a formal counterexample to the unrestricted statement, as the dispatch's 'strongest true version' asked. At minimum, state in the docstring that the general failure is unproved here.

issues.problem: CAMPAIGN.md defines 'partial' to include 'a reading', and the row records a reading of :1156 ('loop in X' read as 'loop in U') together with a finding that :1156 as written is wrong (literally it makes the necessary-and-sufficient claim false, e.g. for S^1). The dispatch itself defines SLSC the Hatcher way and the paper's own :1451-1456 agree, so the formal content is sound. Only the status label is in tension with the protocol.
issues.fix: Either mark the row 'partial (reading of :1156)' or have the master record explicitly that the dispatch's definition supersedes the :1156 wording, keeping 'closed'.

issues.problem: There is no uniqueness-up-to-isomorphism statement: a covering q : E -> Y with E simply connected (and LPC) is homeomorphic over Y to UniversalCover Y y0. The paper uses this at :1156 ('admit a universal covering') and in the proof of prop:universality at :1185-1186 ('maximal among covering of Y\S hence its universal covering'). Downstream Fox-completion packages will need it. existsUnique_lift, isCoveringMap_of_comp_eq and lift_surjective give the maximality half only.
issues.fix: Add e.g. UniversalCover.homeomorphOfSimplyConnected : (E simply connected, q covering, q e0 = y0) -> UniversalCover Y y0 homeo E commuting with proj/q and sending base to e0. Build it from the two lifts and existsUnique uniqueness.

Both are disclosed in notes/extra_decls.

summary: The file builds clean with 0 sorry and standard axioms only. The construction is genuine and every dispatch item is proved: SLSC, the universal cover with its basis topology, the covering endpoint map, path-connected/simply connected/LPC total space, the universal property (with the lift itself a covering), Deck as a subgroup with Deck = pi_1 via an explicit action, composition under finite fibres, and countable pi_1. Statements are at least as strong as the paper's, every weakening is reported, and the hypotheses are satisfiable (checked at Y = R). One major issue: REPORT wrongly says the paper states no composition result, while :1137 uses an unrestricted 'composition of coverings is a covering', which is false in general and is not served by the finite-fibre version. The other issues are minor: a status/reading tension, missing uniqueness-up-to-iso API, namespace/global-instance hygiene, a universe restriction in the iff, and naming.
